newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Leftist group challenges Manila to APEC debate.
newsitem.headline: Leftist group challenges Manila to APEC debate.

text.p: A leftist group at the forefront of opposition to the APEC summit on Friday challenged the Philippine government to a public debate, saying it would prove the trade bloc was anti-poor.
"The Manila People's Forum has issued a challenge (for) a televised public debate to the Ramos Administration," Walden Bello, chairman of the committee, said at a news conference.

Bello, a professor at the University of the Philippines, said the forum disputed the position taken by APEC officials that free trade and complete deregulation would guarantee sustained economic growth.
He said he had thrown down the gauntlet to Philippine ministers and the U.S. representative to APEC, John Wolf, among others. No one had taken up the challenge, he said.

The Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum is due to hold its annual summit meeting in the Philippines with senior officials and ministers meeting separately between November 20 and 22. The leaders will meet on November 25.

To express opposition to APEC's goals of freeing trade and investments in the region, the Manila People's Forum has organised a counter-APEC forum to which it invited several delegates from abroad, including Nobel peace prize winner and East Timorese resistance leader Jose Ramos Horta.
But the Philippine government has denied a visa to Ramos Horta, saying his presence could disrupt the APEC meeting.
The government has also denounced the leftists as troublemakers who want to capitalise on the media attention that would be focused on the country during the APEC summit.

"What we are doing here is really ventilating issues and trying to project the position of the civil society ... We think there is a closing down of all opportunities for people outside of the official quarters to say something about APEC," said Horacio Morales, another leading member of the People's Forum.

"(The government) are saying we are interesting (to the press) because we are raising issues about East Timor, human rights and all other issues which are not central to the main question of economic liberalisation. Of course, we disagree with this," he added.
"We would like to....bring the focus of this discussion around APEC -- the real, hard economic liberalisation issues," Bello said.
Three other forums against APEC have been scheduled ahead of the APEC summit on November 25. Protest caravans to the summit site have also been planned by the organisers.

APEC groups Australia, Brunei, Canada, Chile, China, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, Mexico, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, the Philippines, Singapore, Taiwan, Thailand and the United States.
